title: Crew behavioral health on multi-year isolated missions
bottleneck: A Mars mission confines 4-6 people in a small habitat for roughly 1,000 days with up to 20-minute communication delays — no real-time conversation with Earth, no evacuation, no privacy. Analog missions (HI-SEAS, Mars500, Concordia) show conflicts, depression, and performance dips emerging unpredictably, and selection cannot fully screen for it. Countermeasures like virtual reality and structured schedules are untested at mission scale, and a serious psychiatric crisis mid-transit has no good resolution.
why_it_blocks: Hardware gets the attention, but crew dysfunction can end a mission as surely as an engine failure; it is the least modelable risk in the architecture.
current_state: NASA's Human Research Program studies isolation in analogs, including year-long CHAPEA Mars simulations. No actual multi-year deep-space crew isolation has occurred.
